reference.title: Barbell Preacher Curl
reference.listing: Animated GIF (title and number from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.load: Load is user-chosen: the pad removes body swing and the bottom is hardest, so expect less than for a standing barbell curl; pick a bar you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion).

cues.text: Set the seat so the armpits rest on the top of the pad; sit tall, chest against the pad, feet flat. Underhand grip about shoulder width, the backs of the upper arms flat on the pad, arms nearly straight.
Breathe out and curl the bar up; the elbows and upper arms stay on the pad.
Squeeze with the forearms about vertical; do not let the shoulders roll forward or lift off the pad.
Breathe in and lower slowly, 2-3 s, until the arms are nearly straight; keep control at the bottom.
Arms nearly straight, not locked or hanging off the pad; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping into the bottom and bouncing out of it
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly and stop just short of locking the elbows; the stretched bottom is where the elbow is most exposed.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the elbows or the chest off the pad to finish the rep
mistakes.fix: Lighten the bar; the upper arms stay on the pad the whole time.

mistakes.mistake: Seat too low or too high (armpits not on the top of the pad)
mistakes.fix: Adjust the seat so the pad sits in the armpits and the upper arms lie flat on it.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists curling back under the load
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight and grip the bar firmly.

kinematics.norm: Full range from nearly straight arms to about 120-130 degrees; mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across standing barbell, EZ-bar and dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: Supinated grip: the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: Shoulder flexed with the upper arm on the pad: preacher curls load the elbow flexors at short muscle lengths compared with shoulder-extended curls (Attarieh 2025)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm on the pad (rig shapes)
kinematics.norm: Upper arms and elbows stay on the pad throughout (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)

cautions: Elbow: the bottom of a preacher curl stretches the biceps and the front of the elbow under load; lower slowly and stop short of locking out (clinical opinion).
A straight bar turns the forearms fully up; if the wrists or elbows complain, use an EZ bar (clinical opinion).
Take the bar from the bench hooks or a partner and put it back the same way; do not let it roll off the pad.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: One dumbbell at a time (dumbbell preacher curl).
regressions: Empty bar or a light fixed barbell.
Shorter range: stop the lowering at about 30 degrees of elbow bend.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor and forearm supinator; a supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023). The pad fixes the upper arm in front of the body, so the shoulder cannot swing the bar.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) helps flex the elbow (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the bar and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Keeps the upper arm pressed on the pad (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor and forearm supinator; a supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase (Coratella 2023). The pad fixes the upper arm in front of the body, so the shoulder cannot swing the bar.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) helps flex the elbow (Coratella 2023).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the bar and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Keeps the upper arm pressed on the pad (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the chest steady against the pad.
